assertions.requirement: Two tracked node pools retain distinct product identities while reporting the one cluster Kubernetes identity and connection revision.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/node-pool.ts: createReadyNodePool and observeNodePoolIsolation.

assertions.requirement: Each node pool reaches the requested capacity with stable host and Kubernetes node identities.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/node-pool.ts: createReadyNodePool and proveCapacityReplacement; substrates/local-cluster/capacity-compute.ts joins each K3s agent container through the production join credential and kubelet drop-in, and contracts/cluster-local.ts checks, once the pools are ready, that every pool Node is Ready, carries the API-set node-restriction.kubernetes.io/anycloud-node-pool label of its pool, and its kubelet configz has singleProcessOOMKill.

assertions.requirement: A Deployment is created in its selected node pool, reaches its exact generation, and produces a Ready Pod.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/deployment.ts: createManagedDeployment and waitForDeploymentReady consume the tracked node pool binding.

assertions.requirement: Every Deployment mutation uses one active parent-bound tracked reference. Creation authorizes the completed allowlisted payload, so extra fields cannot replace its node pool, name, or operation.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/deployment.ts: createManagedDeployment; deployment-mutations.ts: DeploymentMutationTransport; deployments.ts: TrackedDeploymentKernel authorizes each payload against the active parent-bound reference.

assertions.requirement: The Deployment has no native Kubernetes Deployment, Pod, ReplicaSet, Secret, or ServiceAccount resources in the sibling node pool.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/deployment.ts: proveDeploymentIsolation requires all five native resource classes to be absent in the sibling node pool.

assertions.requirement: A named Secret a Deployment references reaches its replica as environment, and the Deployment's status shows the Secret's name but never its value.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/deployment.ts: qualifyDeploymentSecret waits for the replica's SECRET_SHA256 log line and checks the status through probes/named-secret.ts appearsIn; fixtures/deployment.py logs only the digest.

assertions.requirement: Every targeted Job retains its exact Job identity, submission revision, and selected Deployment identity.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: submitJob validates tracked Job and Deployment bindings through targetedJobStatus.

assertions.requirement: A Deployment-targeted Job creates no dedicated VM provisioning row or attempt.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: releaseJob requires one Workload row and zero VM rows before release and recording completion.

assertions.requirement: Bucket workloads targeting a Deployment are rejected before persistence.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyTargetedJobAdmission rejects targeted bucket input before persistence.

assertions.requirement: A targeted Job without a fixture reservation becomes Invalid and cleans up.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyTargetedJobAdmission requires Invalid and persisted cleanup for the missing reservation.

assertions.requirement: Operator resubmission preserves Job identity and advances the durable submission revision exactly once.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyTargetedJobAdmission and qualifyConcurrentTargetedJobs require the same public Job ID and exactly one revision advance.

assertions.requirement: Application retry changes execution identity while retaining Job and Deployment identity.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyApplicationRetry retains the Job through its Retrying event and completion; the retired GPU extension correlates numerical execution evidence.

assertions.requirement: Two submissions start before either is awaited and both claim at revision zero through one installed AsyncClient.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyConcurrentTargetedJobs requires two distinct exact Job IDs claimed at revision zero through one installed AsyncClient; the Python two-admission barrier rejects serialization.

assertions.requirement: Successful concurrent submission records zero pending tasks and a closed SDK transport.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyConcurrentTargetedJobs consumes the closed-transport and zero-pending-task observation emitted by the Python driver finalizer.

assertions.requirement: An occupied Deployment expires an unclaimed submission without later starting it, while a blocking submission waits for capacity.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyConcurrentTargetedJobs proves saturation, first-claim expiry, blocking admission, and same-ID renewal.

assertions.requirement: Completing one Job closes only its watcher while another active Job continues waiting for cancellation.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyConcurrentTargetedJobs proves completion closes only that Job watcher while the second Job remains active.

assertions.requirement: Job termination observes cancellation acknowledgement and watcher shutdown before releasing capacity and cleanup.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyConcurrentTargetedJobs requires cancellation acknowledgement and watcher closure before Job release.

assertions.requirement: A lost successful admission reply recovers the original Job and revision without a second admission or execution.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: proveSubmissionResponseLoss admission stage.

assertions.requirement: A lost successful claimed-observation reply recovers the original Job and revision without resubmission.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: proveSubmissionResponseLoss observation stage.

assertions.requirement: Both response-loss paths retain the exact tracked Job and Deployment references, one running container, one execution, one work start, and stable Pod/container/image identity.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: proveSubmissionResponseLoss and responseLossExecutionViolation preserve tracked references and exact execution, Pod, container, and image identities.

assertions.requirement: Response-loss evidence binds source, API, installed SDK wheel, workflow attempt, closed transport, and zero pending tasks.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: proveSubmissionResponseLoss; python-sdk.ts: WorkspacePythonSdk artifactIdentity and startSubmissionResponseLoss validate identity, recovery and session closure before release.

assertions.requirement: Hard API-process replacement changes controller instance while preserving endpoint, node pool, Deployment, and live Job identity. Cloud recovery also waits for public DNS to identify the exact new Running native VM and reloads raw-TLS Kubernetes access across the replacement.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/node-pool.ts: replaceClusterController and confirmClusterConnection require a new controller and unchanged node pool/cluster identities. The cloud environment rejects access acquired across replacement, excludes stale DNS addresses, and probes the recovered native endpoint.

assertions.requirement: Deleting the Deployment Pod produces a new Pod identity without changing Deployment generation or losing targeted work.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/deployment.ts: replaceDeploymentPod requires a new Ready Pod at the existing generation; the composition passes that observation to targeted Job redelivery.

assertions.requirement: Updating the Deployment environment advances its generation, drains old work, and exposes the new configuration only from the replacement Pod.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/deployment.ts: beginDeploymentRollout preserves the active Pod while draining; finishDeploymentRollout requires the exact active Job cleanup proof and a new Pod at the desired generation.

assertions.requirement: A terminal Job awaiting persisted cleanup continues occupying its Deployment slot until cleanup is recorded.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: startTargetedRuntimeLoss and finishTargetedRuntimeLoss fence slot reuse across terminal state, Pod replacement, and persisted cleanup.

assertions.requirement: A targeted Job whose handler allocates past its Deployment's --memory retries with the reason "replica OOMKilled (exit 137)", keeps the killed attempt's replica log tail, and its next claim completes it (RFC 0044 S17).
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyReplicaOomRetry reads the attempt's stored tail through the local facts server; fixtures/deployment.py allocates past the one-slot Deployment's memory limit set in contracts/cluster-local.ts.

assertions.requirement: A replica Pod carries the anycloud finalizer, runs the existing image under RuntimeDefault seccomp without privilege escalation and isn't BestEffort, and a drained rollout releases it within 20 s of its container stopping (RFC 0044 S18, K6, K9).
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/deployment.ts: proveHardenedReplica and proveReplicaReleased on the rollout in contracts/cluster-local.ts, reading whole Pods from the API.

assertions.requirement: node pool deletion is rejected while either tracked child Deployment remains live.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/deployment.ts: proveNodePoolDeletionFence requires NODE_POOL_REFERENCED before child deletion.

assertions.requirement: Each Anycloud Deployment has a durable deletion record and independent zero counts for native Kubernetes Deployments, Pods, ReplicaSets, Secrets, and ServiceAccounts before release. Resource absence comes from canonical HTTP status; quoted body codes cannot turn authorization or transport failures into absence.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/deployment.ts: deleteDeployment consumes durable deletion and all five exact native absence observations; kubernetes-observations.ts: deploymentAbsent; kubernetes-client.ts: kubernetesStatusCode.

assertions.requirement: Fallback teardown uses independent SDK, process, polling, and uncached Kubernetes-client acquisition even after foreground access is warm or cancelled. Bounded API-unavailable read retries require a complete terminal response, preserve successful SDK finalization and the original abort scope, and never replay a mutation; unresolved identity or incomplete native absence retains child/parent tracking and unconfirmed qualification cleanup.
assertions.candidateEvidence: deployments.ts: TrackedDeploymentKernel retries only classified read observations and retains unresolved children; context.ts supplies an independent cleanup transport, WorkspacePythonSdk and KubernetesQualificationTransport.

assertions.requirement: Each node pool records deletion and independently releases all capacity before its tracked reference is released.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/node-pool.ts: deleteNodePools preserves capacity history, confirms zero live capacity and Node absence on the cluster, then releases the tracked node pool.

assertions.requirement: Concurrent resource releases and reservations preserve every live cleanup manifest entry. Failed manifest operations retain tracking and do not prevent later resources from being persisted.
assertions.candidateEvidence: cleanup-manifest.ts: CleanupManifest serializes tracked Deployment, node pool and Workload manifest operations; node-pools.ts and deployments.ts own their manifests.

assertions.requirement: An exec probe blocks queued work during warmup and readiness loss; recovery admits waiting Jobs without releasing active executions. Probe-only updates and explicit removal replace the native configuration; unconfigured application readiness remains unknown.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyNativeReadiness retains prequeued warmup and recovery. contracts/deployment.ts: qualifyDeploymentProbeChanges checks probe-only update/removal and unknown unconfigured readiness through the installed SDK and production API.

assertions.requirement: Individual status identifies both old-generation Jobs, then the remaining blocker despite an unused slot. Queued work waits for full release and claims the replacement generation and Pod.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: queueTargetedJobDuringDrain, proveRemainingTargetedBlocker and qualifyReplacementGenerationJob retain both-blocked, one-blocked and replacement snapshots; targets/cluster-node-pool.ts: recordDeploymentDrain.

assertions.requirement: Warmup and readiness recovery wake the same already-waiting next_job request for prequeued work before its deadline, without another Job mutation. Probe detection and probe-to-receive costs are recorded separately.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/targeted-job.ts: proveReadinessWakeup correlates bounded log markers, native probe timestamps and both waiting/returned receive sequences. The success bundle requires distinct warmup and recovery records on the same warm Pod, exact targeted Job identities and the unchanged 19-second/5-second timing assertions.

assertions.requirement: Sibling failure, parent timeout/cancellation, and cooperative SIGTERM join owned requests before closing the installed AsyncClient. Failed or incomplete closure records observed diagnostics and cannot produce a successful result.
assertions.candidateEvidence: fixtures/python-sdk-driver.py: main and process_main own finalization; python-sdk.ts: WorkspacePythonSdk parses the finalization receipt; read-retry.ts: sdkStatus.

assertions.requirement: One composition creates two node pools and two Deployments, binds every distinct targeted Job completion to those resources, and includes separate resource, async, and optional GPU records.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/cluster-local.ts: ClusterLocalContract binds one cluster, two node pools, two Deployments, one node pool Service and 19 targeted Job completions, including warmup/recovery and two-slot drain, after all owner finalizers return.

assertions.requirement: Native Kubernetes observations retry only transient GET failures within one finite budget. Every HTTP attempt and body stream is cancelled at its deadline or settlement. Authentication, schema, identity, and foreground cancellation remain terminal; cleanup retains its independent abort scope and fresh client acquisition.
assertions.candidateEvidence: kubernetes-reads.ts: KubernetesApiReads owns actual SDK request cancellation and GET-only recovery; kubernetes-observations.ts: KubernetesWorkloadObservations consumes it.

assertions.requirement: The runner's K3s server is the cluster's cluster record, written by the API before it serves with the installer-kind connection (a cluster-admin ServiceAccount token plus the server CA, as bootstrap mints it) and the kube-system identity the fixture observed itself; the listed record must carry that identity.
assertions.candidateEvidence: substrates/local-cluster/api-child.ts: recordSelf before serving; substrates/local-cluster/environment.ts: ClusterLocalEnvironment waits for the record to list Ready and compares its identity; substrates/local-cluster/cluster-host.ts: LocalClusterHost, publishedKubeconfig and mintInstallerConnection.

assertions.requirement: Every node pool VM is a K3s agent started from the exact production join configuration: the cluster join endpoint, the CA-pinned bootstrap token, the Node name, labels and taints the node pool controller issued for that attempt.
assertions.candidateEvidence: substrates/local-cluster/capacity-compute.ts: clusterLocalAgentConfigFromStartupScript and createClusterLocalCapacityCompute; test/unit/e2e-local-cluster-substrate.spec.ts round-trips buildNodePoolAgentStartupScript.

assertions.requirement: anycloud service --node-pool runs as Pods on the node pool without a VM row, reaches Running, and its deletion removes the Service-owned namespace on the cluster before the tracked reference is released.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/cluster-local.ts: qualifyNodePoolService; kubernetes-observations.ts: serviceNamespaceAbsent.

assertions.requirement: anycloud logs reads Pods through the API: a running node pool Service shows its container's startup output, and a Deployment shows its newest Pod's output while that Pod's native readiness probe still fails.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/cluster-local.ts: qualifyNodePoolService reads services.logs; contracts/targeted-job.ts: qualifyNativeReadiness reads deploymentCliLogs; transports/node-pool-service.ts: logs; kubernetes-transport.ts: deploymentCliLogs.

assertions.requirement: anycloud exec reaches pool Pods through the API under the chart's RBAC: a Deployment runs the command in its ready replica or the one --replica names, refusing an unknown replica; a running pool Job runs it in the replica holding its claim with the remote exit code, and a Job queued behind it or already ended is refused.
assertions.candidateEvidence: contracts/cluster-local.ts: qualifyDeploymentExec after the Deployment is ready, qualifyPoolJobExec on the second node pool; kubernetes-transport.ts: exec.

assertions.requirement: Deleting every node pool leaves the cluster Ready under its original Kubernetes identity with its K3s server still running; only node pool Nodes and agent containers disappear.
assertions.candidateEvidence: substrates/local-cluster/environment.ts: clusterIntact and nodePoolAbsent; contracts/cluster-local.ts: ClusterLocalContract.run.

assertions.requirement: A hard API-process replacement while a targeted Job is active reconstructs node pool, Deployment and Job state from the durable ledger: the cluster connection revision, node pool VM rows and the running Job are unchanged afterwards.

assertions.requirement: After a Service on a node pool reaches Running, `anycloud wait <id> --json` exits 0 with a ready state record.

assertions.requirement: A Helm-managed API built from this tree, naming its chart published to a registry beside K3s and installed with an older inline chart that lacks the pods/log rule (what an upgrade from a release before 0.1.68 leaves) and selects the management label the Node sets itself, switches the HelmChart to its own digest-pinned OCI chart at start: its ServiceAccount gains pods/log, the HelmChart names that chart with no inline content, and the one replacement API Pod runs Ready on node-restriction.kubernetes.io/anycloud-management, which create and api upgrade set, finds its chart current and is neither replaced nor restarted.

assertions.requirement: With its own kubelet credential, a pool Node that admits privileged Jobs can label itself, but not with node-restriction.kubernetes.io/anycloud-node-pool or anycloud-management or node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, and the K3s supervisor issues it a kubelet certificate for its own Node name but refuses one for the next attempt's Node name.
assertions.candidateEvidence: substrates/local-cluster/kubelet-restrictions.ts: assertKubeletRestrictions, called by contracts/cluster-local.ts once the node pools are ready.
